result.topic_en: Gauss computes auxiliary angles via sine relations with tabulated logarithmic constants g, h for a worked example (φ = 51°31'48"), then introduces auxiliary angles U defined by a tan U = b tan T and derives trigonometric relations between T, U, T', U'.
result.transcription:
Die Winkel finden sich
$\sin 2u = g \sin T$
$\sin T' = \frac{h \sin T}{\cos u^2}$

$g \ldots 8.9095925$ $h$ $9.9992822$
$g' \ldots 7.2185606$ $h'$ $9.9999996$
$g'' \ldots 3.8350620$ $h''$ $0$

z.B. $51.31.48 = \varphi$
$0.09986$
$00144$
$38.33.46 = T$
$\sin T$ $9.79475$
$8,90959$
$9.99928$
$2u \ldots 2.54.4$
$9.79403$
$28$
$\sin T'$ $9.79431$
$T' = 38.31.0$

Man führe noch ein
$a \,\mathrm{tg}\, U = b \,\mathrm{tg}\, T$
$a' \,\mathrm{tg}\, U' = b' \,\mathrm{tg}\, T'$
$a'' \,\mathrm{tg}\, U'' = b'' \,\mathrm{tg}\, T''$
Dann ist
$\sin T' = \frac{\sin \frac{1}{2}(T+U)}{\cos \frac{1}{2}(T-U)}$
$\cos U' = \frac{a \sin T'}{a' \,\mathrm{tg}\, T} = \frac{b \sin T'}{a' \,\mathrm{tg}\, U} = \frac{b' \sin T'}{a' \sqrt{\mathrm{tg}\, T \,\mathrm{tg}\, U}}$
[-$\sin \frac{1}{2}(T'-U') \cdot \sin \frac{1}{2}(T'+U') = \frac{\sin(T'-T)}{\sin T}$-]
[-$\cos \frac{1}{2}(T'-U') \cdot \cos \frac{1}{2}(T'+U') = \frac{\sin(T'+T)}{\sin T}$-]
[-$\sin U' = \frac{\cos T'}{\sqrt{\mathrm{tg}\, T \,\mathrm{tg}\, U}}$-]
[-$a' \sin U' = \frac{b b' \sin T'^2}{}$-]
[-$\sin 2U' = \frac{b' \sin 2T'}{a' \,\mathrm{tg}\, T}$-]
[-$a' \cos T'$-] $b' \cos T' = \frac{a \sin U'}{\mathrm{tg}\, T}$
$b' \cos T' = \frac{b \sin U'}{\mathrm{tg}\, U}$
Gut. $\cos T' = \frac{\sin U'}{\sqrt{\mathrm{tg}\, T \cdot \mathrm{tg}\, U}}$
